resources.string: Projection: r = R × (90° − elevation) / 90°, azimuth clockwise from true north; outer ring = horizon (0°), center = zenith (90°). Filled with a white core = satellite used in the fix.
Off-sky satellites (el < 5° or invalid angle; not plotted)
No satellite data — recovers automatically after the warning above is resolved
Waiting for the system GNSS status callback…
Format: constellation SVID · EL elevation · AZ azimuth · CN0 C/N0 · ● used in fix

Data note: satellite azimuth, elevation, CN0 and fix participation are actual values reported by the Android GnssStatus callback — not estimated, not simulated. The zenith plot expresses only the geometric position of satellites in the sky, not distance. There is no data when location is off, precise-location permission is missing, or the device has no GNSS hardware. CN0 below %1$d dB-Hz is a weak signal and fix quality may degrade.
